glosses: Resembling or characteristic of a rat; ratlike.

examples.text: I was having exactly that thought on a ratty mock-leather couch in Islington.

We got an old tin lantern, and a butcher knife without any handle, and a bran-new Barlow knife worth two bits in any store, and a lot of tallow candles, and a tin candlestick, and a gourd, and a tin cup, and a ratty old bed-quilt off the bed, […] and just as we were leaving I found a tolerable good curry-comb, and Jim he found a ratty old fiddle-bow, and a wooden leg.
The Marcher lord was still clad in his ratty black cloak and dented breastplate with its chipped enamel lightning.

glosses: Crazy, mad; ridiculous; slightly strange, eccentric; also (followed by about, on, or over), attracted to, infatuated with.

examples.text: He got bad, he got ratty, he would take it out on people around him. He was mean when it turned against him.

translations.source_sense_description: similar to a rat — see also ratlike

glosses: Synonym of knock down ginger (“prank of knocking on a front door and running away”).
